newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to record close.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2404 +25 US 30yr cl 6.43 -0.03
*Stocks end at record close. ANZ result, BHP rent tax deal send market higher in afternoon. Volume 435.15 million shares, value A$790.90 million, 1,108 stocks traded, 345 steady, 474 up, 289 down.
Australian shares sprinted home to a record close on Wednesday as an afternoon rally pushed an already Dow-inspired market to higher territory.
A positive profit result from ANZ Bank and a surge in bellwether BHP after settlement of a tax dispute lit the fuse, pushing the key sharemarket barometer further ahead.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 26.7 points at 2,392.7 after reaching an intraday high of 2394.7, some 3.9 points off its record high.
December share price index futures were 25 points higher at 2,404, a 9.3 point premium to the underlying index.

"The banks and the top miners are the ones that have pulled the market along today," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd. "The result from ANZ Bank was good and that has fuelled the banks along," he said, citing strong performances from Westpac and National Australia Bank as well as ANZ.

ANZ posted a 6.7 percent higher full year net profit of A$1.12 billion. In the resources sector, BHP was the star in a day of strong performances, its shares surging to end over three percent higher after it settled the resource rent tax dispute.
The market leader said the dispute settlement would see a A$167 million benefit to its bottom line.
"That's been a big plus for BHP," Tredenick said.

Property developer and financial services group Lend Lease also attracted attention, its shares moving to record highs as investors bought into the tightly held company for its strong growth prospects.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trading was active, tracking movements in the major miners, BHP especially.
Total options traded 56,211 (28,342)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 8,173 (6,408)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields were held to a narrow range just above last week's 33-month lows with the market finding difficulty in making further progress in the absence of any key local data. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were yielding 7.11 percent.
The Australian dollar reinforced its rally with another 1/4 cent of gains Wednesday as supporters elbowed aside resistance at US$0.7960 to snatch their third chart scalp of the week.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$7959/64.
